observed.facings.png: A single picture labelled south. It shows a rusty, patched pump assembly. Toward the back-left is a grey centrifugal pump volute. A vertical riser rises from it to a bolted top flange whose open mouth is seen from above as an ellipse, with rope wrapped around the neck. An elbow pipe on the left drops down into the front pipe. A grey ribbed electric motor with rust patches sits on a wooden skid to the right. Wooden braces and timber feet hold it together, and a rope lashing is tied near the right end. A long horizontal manifold pipe runs across the front. Both of its ends finish in bolted flanges seen edge-on as narrow vertical discs, with no opening visible. The background is a transparent checkerboard.
observed.south.png: The same picture at full resolution on a transparent background. The painting is clean, with a dark outline and painterly rust and metal shading. The west and east manifold flanges are edge-on with bolt heads along their rims. The only open bore is on the top flange of the vertical riser, and it faces upward. There is no stub on the south side.
observed.scale.png: The station on brown ground beside a vanilla human at the same scale. It is about 2.5 times the pawn's width and a bit taller than the pawn. There is no backdrop or shadow.
observed.siblings.png: The in-game capture of the repaired sibling: a red and cream station with red valve wheels, white manifold pipes and a dark motor, with a hose running south from the bottom centre. The camera and size class are similar to this candidate's.
observed.assembled_1.png: In-game capture with the candidate swapped in. The manifold ends are edge-on flanges, so the pipe no longer looks bent toward the viewer. A C#-drawn stub drops from below the centre of the manifold, between the wooden feet, to a brass coupler and a wrapped hose going south. A loose hose end lies in the grass on the right and is not attached. The machine draws over the ground and stub.
observed.assembled_2.png: The kept original in game. Its west and east manifold ends show large open bores facing the camera, which makes the horizontal pipe look turned toward the viewer. There is a power-off lightning icon. The stub and coupler at the bottom centre are the same as in assembled_1.

CAMERA.seen: The riser's top flange is an ellipse about 0.55–0.6 as tall as it is wide, with its lit inner face visible. The skid's top is shown above its front band. The motor and pipes sit at a consistent elevated angle, and the camera matches the sibling.

BORE.seen: The only open bore is at the top of the vertical riser, which really points up toward the camera. The horizontal manifold's west and east ends are now edge-on flanges with no visible opening.

PORTS.seen: In assembled_1 the C#-drawn south stub comes straight down from below the centre of the manifold to the brass coupler and hose, in the same plane and at the same cell. No hose is attached to the side ports in this capture. The loose hose end on the right is game-drawn and unattached.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: The west and east manifold ends carry bolted flange connectors. The south stub and coupler are drawn by C#, as the card says, and appear at the bottom centre. The riser's top flange is not listed as a port, but it reads as the pump's discharge or riser flange, part of the defining description ('a vertical riser with a top flange') rather than a hose connector.

LAYERS.seen: The machine draws over the stub's upper end and over the ground. The stub and coupler sit below and in front of the skid with no wrong overlap.

ROTATIONS.seen: Graphic_Single: one picture for every rotation, by design.

SIGNATURE.seen: All the described parts are visible: the vertical riser with its top flange, the front manifold running west-east, the borrowed electric motor, mismatched rust patch plates and rope lashings.

MATERIAL.seen: Rusted steel, cast iron, worn timber and hemp rope all read as materials, with no flat paint coat.

FOOTPRINT.seen: About 451 px of visible height on the 3x3 canvas. The machine fills the width with small margins and does not overflow.

ALPHA.seen: Real alpha with a transparent background. There is no ground patch or cast shadow.

OURS.seen: A bespoke painted kludged station that is not vanilla art. It is an edit of the kept own art.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell the silhouette of pump, motor and manifold pipe stays distinct, and the edge-on end flanges read as pipe ends.

proposals: Consider a slight ellipse or rim highlight on the edge-on west and east flanges so that, once side hoses attach in game, the side ports read clearly as hose connection points at 32 px per cell.

observed.facings.png: An enlarged view of the Scrapper candidate. A round piece with a broad dark brown-grey outer ring. Inside it is a thin pale tan ring, then a recessed disc shaded from lighter warm brown on the left to darker on the right, with a thin black crescent on the right inner rim. It looks like a shallow cup or a recess seen face-on. The background is transparent.
observed.south.png: The same Scrapper piece at 64x64: a dark round disc with a faint lighter inner ring. Its edges are clean against transparency and it nearly fills the canvas.
observed.scale.png: In-game crops of three hose reels (red Modern, black and yellow Industrial, rusty Scrapper), each with its hose laid east, and a vanilla human to the right for scale. The right column shows each hose's free end: a wrapped or clamped tip ending in a small dark oval opening.
observed.variants_1.png: Industrial candidate: an almost black disc with a thin grey rim, a slightly lighter dark ring inside, and a very dark centre. It reads as black rubber.
observed.variants_2.png: Modern candidate: a pale grey-beige outer ring with a dark outline, a dark brown-grey inner recess shaded darker toward the lower right, and a thin dark inner crescent.
observed.variants_3.png: Futuristic candidate: a pale grey-white rim with four short cyan glowing arcs, then a cyan inner ring around a dark grey recess with a faint fine dot texture.
observed.assembled_1.png: The in-game crop with the candidates pasted in. At each hose tip (right column) a narrow vertical ellipse caps the end. The Modern (top) end shows a pale ring around a light grey interior with a small dark edge, so it reads almost like a pale cap or plug. The Industrial (middle) end is a dark ring with a slightly lighter grey interior. The Scrapper (bottom) end is a pale grey ring around a dark centre. Each sits at the tip, in the hose's plane, and is the same size as the original.
observed.assembled_2.png: The same crop with the original Mouth art. Each hose tip shows a near-black oval hole with a thin rim: a strongly open, deep-looking bore.

CAMERA.seen: The piece is squashed by C# to a narrow vertical ellipse at the tip (assembled_1). Within that ellipse the texture shades as a shallow recess and adds no extra perspective of its own.

BORE.seen: The bore shows only at the hose's cut end, as a narrow ellipse in the plane the C# sets. The interior is now graded and lighter than the near-black hole in assembled_2, so it no longer reads as a pipe bent up toward the viewer. The open end is shown at all only because the description asks for it.

PORTS.seen: In assembled_1 each pasted Mouth sits exactly on its hose tip, at the same height and angle as the game's original.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: The single code port (the free end) has the open-end piece drawn at the tip. The piece adds no other connectors.

LAYERS.seen: The Mouth draws over the wrap and the hose tip, as it should.

ROTATIONS.seen: There is one texture per look, rotated by the C#. The four looks share one construction (rim, recess, inner crescent) and differ only in material.

SIGNATURE.seen: Each piece reads as an open hose end with a rim and a recess. The Modern one in assembled_1 is pale enough to verge on a capped end.

MATERIAL.seen: Scrapper reads as worn brown rubber, Industrial as black rubber, Modern as a pale fabric or rubber rim, Futuristic as a light shell with cyan emissive.

FOOTPRINT.seen: The measured visible alpha height is 62 px of 64, so the piece fills the canvas. Size and placement are set by C#.

ALPHA.seen: All four pieces have clean transparent corners: no backdrop and no halo.

OURS.seen: Each piece is derived from its look's own Mouth art. No donor art.

LEGIBLE.seen: At normal zoom the tip reads as the hose end, a small oval cap. The interior detail is lost, which is acceptable for a piece this small.

request.prompt: A short piece of the open free end of a hose lying flat on the ground, for a top-down RimWorld sprite, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline, transparent background. The hose is seen from a slightly raised viewpoint, and the end lies in the ground plane. The cut end is seen nearly edge-on: a thin pale cut-wall rim runs around the hose's end, with only a narrow sliver of the near-side inner wall showing below it. Inside the rim the opening is a clearly dark open cavity, a deep charcoal-to-near-black hollow far darker than the hose body and the pale rim, so the end reads as open hose with a deep bore. Just inside the near lip a thin graded band of shading steps from mid grey down to near-black within the first third of the opening, then the dark holds and deepens along the laid hose, giving obvious hollow depth that stays readable when the sprite is small. The rim, shaft and mouth share one flat plane on the ground, so the tip reads as resting on the floor along the hose's length. Ribbed rubber-and-fabric hose body in the look's material colour (rust-streaked patched scrapper hose, black industrial rubber, red moulded modern hose, or sleek futuristic composite), with a worn metal collar behind the cut. Soft contact shadow beneath. Keep the colour palette, material, rim and collar details of the previous render; Scrapper and Industrial keep their material rims. The end face is a thin pale cut wall ringing a dark shaded recess with graded shading, with no flat fill and no concentric seam rings.
